title: NorthStar Rapid Deployment Proposal + Workshop Log
content:
Context:
NorthStar (fintech analytics) wants a short POC to validate an ML-powered assistant that summarizes earnings calls and answers regulatory/financial questions over their internal docs. They need a path to production that meets compliance and predictable cost targets. This doc captures the deployment proposal, agreed workshop notes (Nov 4/2025 design workshop), and concrete success criteria for go/no-go decisions.

Primary objectives for the 6-week engagement:
- Deliver an end-to-end integration that ingests a subset of NorthStar docs and exposes a QA + summarization endpoint to their UI.
- Demonstrate latency & cost targets under realistic traffic (20 concurrent users, peak burst to 60 concurrent).
- Surface quality metrics vs. baseline (current keyword search + heuristic summarizer).
- Produce an operational runbook and rollback plan for the next 90-day pilot.

Customer constraints & must-haves (from kickoff):
- Data residency: production must run in AWS eu-west-1 or on-prem. For POC, limited dataset is ok in hosted sandbox if encrypted in transit & at rest.
- No PII leakage: must show data handling and KMS integration.
- Streaming responses preferred for UI perceived latency.
- Integrate with their SSO (SAML) and existing audit logging.

Proposed technical approach (phased):
Phase 0 (Week 0, pre-engagement):
- Provide dev sandbox credentials (hosted API) and a short quickstart with sample prompts and embedding index.
- Customer shares 200 de-identified docs and a 50-query eval set.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): PoC baseline on Redwood hosted API
- Run model exploration: 3 model variants (open-llm-small, open-llm-medium-8q, redwood-flash-lite) to measure latency/quality.
- Implement ingestion pipeline: S3 -> vector store (FAISS) runner in their test account or our sandbox.
- Deliver basic UI integration demo with streaming.

Phase 2 (Weeks 3–4): Dedicated capacity experiment + optimizations
- Move a replica to Redwood Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 to validate SLA and throughput.
- Apply batching (dynamic up to 8), prefix caching for frequent queries, and 8-bit quantization where viable.
- Run load test (20 sustained, 60 burst) and collect p95/p50/p99 latency, token counts, and cost.

Phase 3 (Weeks 5–6): Harden, eval, and runbook
- Run eval harness (customer queries + synthetic variants) to compute accuracy, hallucination, and response quality.
- Finalize rollout proposal: Dedicated -> Private (if required by compliance) with recommended reserved capacity.

Deployment recommendation summary:
- Short term (fastest): Hosted API sandbox for integration & UX validation (low setup friction).
- Near term (production trial): Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1 with a small reserved pool (2 x A100 equivalent nodes) and burst settings. This gives predictable latency and isolation.
- Long term (regulatory): Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) if audit/trust requirements demand it.

Key performance targets (POC acceptance):
- Latency: interaction p95 <= 350ms for 512-token responses when served from Dedicated; p95 <= 700ms on hosted sandbox remote (network variance allowed).
- Throughput: sustain 20 req/s for 512-token average while keeping p95 < 500ms.
- Error rate: < 1% 5xx for inference calls under load.
- Cost: inference unit economics target <= $1.20 per 1k generated tokens at Dedicated scale (with batching + quant).
- Quality: end-to-end QA accuracy >= 82% vs annotated eval set; hallucination rate <= 3% on sample queries.

Quality and evaluation plan:
- Customer provides a 50-query eval set and 200 human-annotated expected answers. We will run blind evals across 3 model variants.
- Metrics: exact-match/EM, fuzzy-precision (ROUGE-L / BLEU for summaries), hallucination flag rate, and human-rated helpfulness (1–5).
- Regression alert: any drop >5 points in human-rated helpfulness compared to the best baseline triggers a hold and triage.

Workshop (2025-11-04) notes / decisions made:
Attendees: Asha (RWI SE), Diego (RWI Solutions), Priya (Customer Eng), Ethan (Customer Infra), Maya (Product)
- Agreed to start on Hosted API sandbox for first 2 weeks.
- Customer to anonymize PII and share sample dataset by Nov 7.
- Decision: streaming + function-calling to be used for cite/metadata retrieval.
- Logging: both request/response traces and redacted user payloads must go to customer ELK; RWI will forward structured logs via our webhook.
- SSO integration deferred to Week 4 (post-demo).

Open questions (action items):
- Q1: Do they need model residency in their VPC for legal BEFORE any testing? (Owner: Priya, due 2025-11-06)
- Q2: Are there rate limits on their side for ingestion from S3? (Owner: Ethan, due 2025-11-06)
- Q3: Which teams will be the sign-off stakeholders for the final acceptance? (Owner: Priya, due 2025-11-09)

Risk register and mitigations:
- Data leakage risk: mitigate via strict redaction rules, KMS encryption, and test set de-id. If unresolved, move to Private deployment.
- Cost overrun: mitigate by early quantization and monitoring; set auto-thresholds for burst caps.
- Latency spikes due to cold KV cache: add warmup jobs and pre-warm frequently used prefixes. Monitor cold-starts per node.

Operational runbook highlights (to be delivered week 6):
- Canary rollout steps (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error rate > 2% or p95 > target.
- Monitoring dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per minute, cost per token, cache hit ratio, 5xx rates.
- Escalation path: SE on-call -> Infra SRE -> Product -> Customer success with RACI and 30-minute SLA for Sev1 during pilot.

Acceptance checklist (go/no-go):
- [ ] Ingestion pipeline operational for provided dataset (index size verified).
- [ ] Demo UI shows streaming summarization and QA flows.
- [ ] Latency & throughput targets met in Dedicated load test.
- [ ] Eval metrics meet quality thresholds (see above).
- [ ] Security review completed; KMS integration validated.
- [ ] Rollout & rollback documented and validated in dry-run.

Cost & resource estimates for Dedicated trial:
- Initial reserved pool: 2 nodes (A100 equiv) for 30 days. Estimated cost: $18k–$26k/mo (gross), amortized for POC.
- Expected token volume (est): 5M tokens over POC; recommend early batching and caching to keep per-token costs within target.

Notes for product/engineering handoff:
- Provide the prompt templates and caching keys used during POC.
- Tag model and runtime config (quantization, batching) that met target for reproducibility.
- Include evaluation harness code & anonymized eval results in GitHub repo.

Decisions and next steps (as of 2025-11-04):
- Priya to deliver anonymized dataset and stakeholder list by Nov 7.
- RWI (Asha/Diego) to provision hosted sandbox creds and starter quickstart by Nov 6.
- Load test plan and Dedicated sizing estimate to be completed by Nov 10 (Owner: Diego).
- Follow-up workshop scheduled Nov 17 to review first-week results and select model variant for Dedicated run.

Misc notes / scratch ideas (informal):
- Try a hybrid route: small Dedicated pool for inference + hosted control plane to keep deployment time short.
- Consider incremental embedding refresh (only changed docs) to reduce ingestion work.
- If customer cares about hard real-time (<200ms), explore using a trimmed-context model and aggressive caching.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/northstar-integration
- Sandbox quickstart doc: CONFLUENCE-NS-QUICKSTART-21
- POC contract SOW draft: SOW-NS-2025-v1 (in legal review)

-- end of log --
